nodes.summary: For $n$ wires and an index $i$, this is the comparator on wires $i$ and $i + 1$ when $i + 1 < n$, and nothing when wire $i + 1$ does not exist.
nodes.title: Adjacent comparator

nodes.summary: The bubble network sorts every input over every linear order.
nodes.title: The bubble network sorts

nodes.summary: The bubble sorting network on $n$ wires is the comparator network obtained by concatenating the bubble passes ending at wires $n - 1, n - 2, \ldots, 0$, in this order, where the bubble pass ending at wire $k$ consists of the comparators $(0, 1), (1, 2), \ldots, (k - 1, k)$.
nodes.title: Bubble sorting network

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the bubble sorting network on $n$ wires has $n(n - 1)/2$ comparators: twice its number of comparators is $n(n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Size of the bubble sorting network

nodes.summary: On $n$ wires, for every $m < n$ the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ has exactly $m$ comparators.
nodes.title: Size of a bubble pass

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be an input on $n$ wires with values in a linearly ordered type, let $m < n$, and let $w'$ be the output of the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ (the comparators $(0, 1), \ldots, (m - 1, m)$) run on $w$. Then $w'_i = w_i$ for every wire $i > m$; $w'_i \le w'_m$ for every wire $i \le m$; and for every wire $i \le m$ there is a wire $j \le m$ with $w'_i = w_j$.
nodes.title: Effect of one bubble pass

nodes.summary: On $n$ wires, the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ is the comparator network $(0, 1), (1, 2), \ldots, (m - 1, m)$, applied in this order, where a comparator $(i, i + 1)$ is left out when wire $i + 1$ does not exist (that is, when $i + 1 \ge n$).
nodes.title: Bubble pass

nodes.summary: On $n$ wires and for a number $m$, this is the comparator network obtained by concatenating the bubble passes ending at wires $m - 1, m - 2, \ldots, 0$, in this order; for $m = 0$ it is empty.
nodes.title: Successive bubble passes

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign to each of $n$ wires a value in a linearly ordered type, and let $m$ be a natural number. Then $w$ is settled from $m$ when $w_i \le w_j$ for all wires $m \le i \le j$ (the wires $m, \ldots, n - 1$ are sorted) and $w_i \le w_j$ for all wires $i < m \le j$ (they hold the largest values). This is the invariant before the bubble pass ending at wire $m - 1$.
nodes.title: Settled top wires

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
